name: Astronomical Astrolabe of Ibn al-Shatir
medium_materials: Engraved brass, Inlaid silver, Steel pointer
storage_location: Gallery E - Islamic Science & Cartography, Vitrine 4
description: A brass planispheric astrolabe featuring five interchangeable latitude plates engraved with stereographic projections, an intricate rete adorned with twenty-two stellar pointers, and silver inlay along the alidade.
historical_context: Attributed to the workshops associated with the chief timekeeper (muwaqqit) of the Umayyad Mosque in Damascus, exemplifying fourteenth-century advances in celestial mechanics and solar prayer calculation.
provenance: Documented in the private collection of Dr. Henri de Longperier in Paris from 1892; acquired via auction at Drouot by the Archival Heritage Trust in 1988.
restoration_notes: Surface cleaned in 1990 using micro-crystalline petroleum wax and benzotriazole stabilization on tarnished silver inlay. Rete pivot pinned with archival brass replacement screw.
